title: Tenant-aware priority buckets and escalation playbook for hosted API feature intake
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We receive a growing volume of hosted API feature requests that mix chat streaming, function/tool-calls, and structured-output requirements. The current intake flow buckets requests purely by product area, which causes inconsistent prioritization for enterprise customers with strict SLA/data residency/compliance needs. This ticket defines a tenant-aware prioritization and escalation playbook that maps intake signals to operational policies (routing, dedicated capacity, private deployment recommendation, and SLA-driven escalation).

Goals:
- Create deterministic priority buckets that incorporate tenant contract tier, SLA needs, data residency, PII/regulatory sensitivity, request type (chat streaming, tool calling, structured outputs), expected qps/latency sensitivity, and estimated ARR/strategic value.
- Define automated mapping from bucket -> recommended execution mode (hosted, dedicated, private) and fallback model variants.
- Provide an escalation playbook for high-risk/high-availability enterprise requests (SLA breaches, urgent security/compliance requirements).
- Produce intake scoring logic and a short guidance doc for solutions/SEs to use when assessing inbound requests.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring formula documented and approved by PM, Eng, SRE and Legal: weights for SLA tier, data sensitivity, QPS, latency sensitivity, revenue impact.
Mapping table exists that deterministically maps score ranges and binary signals (PII/regulatory, data residency) to routing decisions: hosted / dedicated / private + fallback policies.
Console intake form updated to capture required signals (expected qps, latency SLO, data residency flag, regulatory tags, estimated ARR, request persona).
Pilot automation: 10 inbound enterprise requests are processed through the scoring flow and resulting routing suggestions are validated by Solutions Engineering within 2 weeks.
Escalation runbook created with contact list, time-to-respond SLAs, and a checklist for ordering Dedicated capacity or Private onboarding.
decision_records: Weighting decision: revenue and SLA sensitivity get highest weights (0.35 each), data residency/PII = 0.2, latency sensitivity = 0.1. Remaining 0.0-0.05 for strategic partnership indicator.

Bucket cutoffs: Score >= 0.8 => Critical enterprise (immediate enterprise intake + recommend Dedicated/Private); 0.6-0.79 => High (fast-track review + recommend Dedicated if sustained qps); 0.4-0.59 => Standard enterprise (hosted by default with monitoring); <0.4 => Developer/self-serve.
Routing policy: Prefer hosted for <0.6 unless data residency/PII/regulatory flags set. Use fallbacks (smaller/quantized models) for cost-constrained buckets but only if latency sensitivity is low.
Security: Any request with regulated data or >= SOC2 Type II requirement must trigger legal & security review and default to Private/Dedicated unless explicit waiver obtained.
